IB CS · SL · Unit 6

Unit 6: Data & Information

SL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How do you structure data so it stays accurate as systems grow?

This unit focuses on relational data design. You will study how databases use tables, keys, and constraints to maintain integrity and reduce redundancy.

You will explain the strengths and limits of relational databases, describe conceptual/logical/physical schema levels, explain how 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF differ, and outline the role of SQL language types: DDL and DML.

Relational structure

Relational systems store data in linked tables.

  • Primary keys identify records uniquely.
  • Foreign keys connect related tables.
  • Referential integrity prevents invalid relationships.
Schema levels

Schemas describe database architecture at different levels:

  • Conceptual: entities and relationships.
  • Logical: fields, keys, and constraints.
  • Physical: DBMS implementation and access strategy.
Normalization

Normalization improves consistency and reduces anomalies:

  • 1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups.
  • 2NF: no partial dependency on a composite key.
  • 3NF: no transitive dependency between non-key fields.
SQL language types

SQL is grouped by purpose:

  • DDL: define/modify structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP).
  • DML: query and update rows (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Relational Database A database that stores linked data in tables using keys and constraints.
Primary Key A field or set of fields that uniquely identifies each record in a table.
Foreign Key A field that references a primary key in another table.
Schema The defined structure of a database and its relationships.
Conceptual Schema A high-level representation of entities and relationships.
Logical Schema Detailed table design including attributes, keys, and constraints.
Physical Schema How the database is implemented in a specific DBMS.
Normalization Organizing tables to reduce redundancy and improve integrity.
1NF / 2NF / 3NF Successive normal forms based on atomicity and dependency rules.
DDL / DML SQL categories for structure management and data manipulation.
